pass1.sentence: hCG is a hormone that begins to be made in the days after fertilisation, as the embryo implants in the womb.
pass1.note: Search summaries: NHS says hCG starts around 6 days after fertilisation; a review says detectable 6-14 days after fertilisation. Made non-numeric and consistent with 'within days of implantation'.

pass1.sentence: a blood test gives a number that normally rises steeply in a healthy early pregnancy.
pass1.note: Review: doubling every 24-48 hours; 'every two days' removed as sources vary (1.94 d average; 29-53 h).

pass1.sentence: Positive from the first day of a missed period; some very sensitive tests can be used earlier.
pass1.note: NHS: most tests can be done from the first day of a missed period; some very sensitive tests before.

pass1.sentence: Modern tests detect low levels of hCG.
pass1.note: '20-25 IU/L' removed: a retrieved source says urine tests typically do not detect below 20 mIU/mL, but it was not a named guideline.

pass1.sentence: NHS advice is to test at least 21 days (three weeks) after the last unprotected sex.
pass1.note: NHS: if you don't know when your next period is due, test at least 21 days after unprotected sex.

pass1.sentence: an ultrasound scan at about 6 to 7 weeks can confirm where the pregnancy is
pass1.note: UHB: early scan usually at about 6-7 weeks by transvaginal ultrasound to confirm fetal heart and intrauterine pregnancy; Tommy's says about 6 weeks.
